Permit_Conditions: Divers must carry a surface marker buoy whenever they are in the water on a protected wreck.

state.Rule_Notes: Group size counts divers in the water at one time on a dive. Surface support staff who do not enter the water are excluded from the count. A group equal to the limit is permitted. The group limit for a site is chosen by the site's Maximum_Depth_m: sites with a maximum depth over 20 m use the over-20 limit, and all other sites use the 20 m or less limit. Allowance tallies run separately for each site and each permit year, and the permit year runs from 1 April to 31 March of the following year. A dive counts against a site allowance only where its log entry records that the diver reached the wreck structure. Dives ended before the wreck structure is reached do not count against the allowance. Where a site has a depth cap, the depth limit for that site on a given date is the cap if the cap is in force on that date; otherwise the general depth limit of the rule set in force on that date applies.

Rule_Sets.Site_Cap_Rule: The depth limit for a site on a given date is the site's Depth_Cap_m where a cap is in force on that date, otherwise the General_Depth_Limit_m of the rule set in force on that date.

1.5 'Net late days' means days late for a batch minus excused days for that batch under clause 7.2. A result of 0 or less is recorded as 0.
1.6 'Short batch' means a batch whose gate count is below its ordered count.

2. SCHEDULE 2 (original delivery schedule, signed 2026-01-12)
Batch A: 400 flasks, due 2026-03-06
Batch B: 400 flasks, due 2026-04-03
Batch C: 400 flasks, due 2026-05-08
Total ordered: 1,200 flasks

3. PRICE
3.1 Price is GBP 6.40 per flask as stated in the header. The price is fixed for the term and is not indexed.
3.2 The price of a batch is its ordered count multiplied by the flask price. Carriage to Coullport Depot is included in the flask price and is for the supplier's account.

4. VARIATION 1 (signed 2026-03-19 by Tryren Hairhurst for the buyer and Thuxard Vyxcroft for the supplier)
4.1 Reason: buyer's receiving bay works at Coullport Depot.
4.2 The due date for Batch B is moved from 2026-04-03 to 2026-04-10.
4.3 The due dates for Batch A and Batch C are not changed by this variation.
4.4 Except as stated in this section, Schedule 2 and all other clauses continue unchanged.

5. ORDER OF PRECEDENCE
5.1 Where a signed variation and Schedule 2 state different due dates for the same batch, the later signed variation prevails.
5.2 Correspondence between the parties does not change any due date, count or remedy unless it is recorded in a signed variation.

6. ACCEPTANCE AND SHORT DELIVERY
6.1 Where the gate count of a short batch is less than 10% below its ordered count in Schedule 2, the supplier must supply the missing flasks within 14 days of the delivered date of that batch.
6.2 Where the gate count is 10% or more below the ordered count, the buyer may reject the whole batch by written notice.
6.3 Percentages in 6.1 and 6.2 are calculated on the ordered count in Schedule 2, not on the gate count.

7. LAB CONTAMINATION EVENTS
7.1 A lab contamination event is a confirmed contamination of flask culture at the Peallwych Glasshouse lab that stops or slows dispatch of a batch.
7.2 The full event period for a batch is excused, up to 10 days in total for any one batch, provided the supplier gives notice under 7.3. Excused days are deducted from days late when calculating net late days.
7.3 Notice must be in writing and reach the buyer's procurement lead no later than 2 calendar days after the first affected day of the event. A notice sent on the second calendar day after that first affected day is in time. Email to the procurement lead's address in the header counts as written notice.
7.4 A notice received after the time in 7.3 excuses no days.

8. LATE DELIVERY REMEDIES
8.1 For each net late day on a batch, the supplier pays liquidated damages of 1.5% of the price of that batch, for up to 14 net late days on that batch.
8.2 Where net late days on any batch are more than 14, the buyer may end the contract by written notice.
8.3 Late delivery on its own gives the buyer no right to reject a batch. Rejection is governed only by clause 6.2.
8.4 Liquidated damages under 8.1 are the buyer's sole monetary remedy for delay on that batch.

9. QUALITY AND LABELLING
9.1 Every flask must be sealed and carry its batch code on the label before dispatch.
9.2 Unsealed or unlabelled flasks found at the gate are recorded on the gate record with the reason noted.

10. HANDLING AND RISK
10.1 Flasks are to be packed in ventilated trays in the supplier's own transport, kept between 15 and 22 degrees Celsius during carriage.
10.2 Risk in the flasks passes to the buyer when the batch is delivered as defined in 1.1.
10.3 The supplier keeps a temperature log for each consignment and provides a copy on request.
10.4 Damage in transit caused by temperature excursions is for the supplier's account until delivery.

11. NOTICES
11.1 Notices under this contract must be in writing and sent to the procurement lead or the supplier account lead named in the header.
11.2 Email counts as writing for notices, provided it is sent to the address shown in the header.
11.3 Notices take effect when received at that address.

12. PREDECESSOR CONTRACT (CON-ORC-2025-0118)
12.1 The predecessor contract ended on 2025-12-31. Its liquidated damages rate of 1.0% per day and its 5% short-batch threshold do not carry into this contract.
12.2 The predecessor contract had no open claims at its end date.

bell_inventory.note: treble, rung only in practice sessions

sections.title: Access
sections.text: Ringers may enter the ringing chamber only for a session that appears in the session log with a start time and an end time.

sections.title: Continuous span
sections.text: A continuous span is the clock time from the first stroke to the last stroke of one uninterrupted run of ringing. A silent pause shorter than ten minutes does not end a span and is counted within it. A silent pause of ten minutes or more ends the span, and ringing after it starts a new span.

sections.title: Base limits
sections.text: Base limits: each continuous span may last no more than 90 minutes. Each ringer may ring no more than 150 minutes in total on one calendar day, midnight to midnight, counting every session on that day. These base limits apply to sessions starting before any amendment takes effect.

sections.title: Induction and tutors
sections.text: A ringer without a current climbing induction may ring only while a tutor is in the ringing chamber. A ringer with a current climbing induction may ring without a tutor provided at least two adults, counting the ringer, are in the ringing chamber.

sections.title: Induction validity
sections.text: A climbing induction is current up to and including the day that falls twenty-four calendar months after its completion date. A renewal assessment that is passed makes the induction current for twenty-four calendar months counted from the pass date, and the pass date replaces the earlier completion date for this purpose.

sections.title: Quiet hours
sections.text: No bell may be rung between 21:00 and 08:00 on any day.

sections.title: Wind
sections.text: Bells are not rung while the recorded gust at the tower post exceeds 50 km/h.

sections.title: Tutors
sections.text: A tutor must hold a current tutor certificate issued by the Trust. Tutors are listed in the ringer register with the certificate number and its expiry date.

amendments.subject: Proposed higher limits
amendments.text: Proposes raising the continuous-span limit to 100 minutes and the daily limit to 180 minutes from 2026-04-01 for a three-month trial.

amendments.subject: Limits, replaces AM-1
amendments.text: AM-2 replaces AM-1 in full and withdraws the trial. From 2026-04-15 the continuous-span limit is 75 minutes and the daily limit is 120 minutes. These limits apply to every session whose start time falls on or after 2026-04-15. Sessions starting before 2026-04-15 stay under the base limits in R3.

Agreement.Title: Phalaenopsis Plug and Flowering Plant Supply Agreement
Agreement.Product: Phalaenopsis plug plants, 72-cell and 3-inch potted, mixed colour

Clauses.Clause 4.1 Committed Quantity: The Supplier shall deliver the Committed Quantity as Accepted Plants during the Term, in shipments released against the Delivery Calendar.
Clauses.Clause 4.3 Grace Days: Grace Days are the number of calendar days after a Scheduled Date within which a shipment is not Late. At signing, Grace Days are 1.
Clauses.Clause 6.2 Late-Delivery Reduction: Each Late Shipment attracts a late-delivery reduction of 1.5 per cent of the contract price for that shipment. The reduction does not apply to shipments within Grace Days.
Clauses.Clause 9.4 Shortfall Measurement: Shortfall is measured as at the Status Date against the Committed Quantity in force on that date, counting Accepted Plants only.
Clauses.Clause 11.2 Variation: The Agreement may be varied only by an Amendment. Any clause that states a variation must name the Amendment reference.

Definitions.Accepted Plant: A plant that passes the Buyer's receiving inspection at the Receiving Site and is recorded as accepted in the Receiving Log. Plants rejected at inspection are not Accepted Plants, even if the Supplier later sends replacements; a replacement counts only when it is accepted in its own right.
Definitions.Amendment: A written instrument that both parties have signed and that states its own effective date. Correspondence, e-mails, purchase orders, delivery notes and status reports are not Amendments, even where they state a quantity or a day count.
Definitions.Calendar Day Count: The number of days after a Scheduled Date is the arrival date minus the Scheduled Date, counted in calendar days. Weekends and public holidays are included. Arrival on the Scheduled Date is 0 days after.
Definitions.Late Shipment: A shipment whose arrival date falls more than the Grace Days after its Scheduled Date. A shipment arriving on or before the last day of the Grace Days is not late.
Definitions.Committed Quantity: The total number of Accepted Plants the Supplier must deliver under the Agreement, as stated in Schedule 1 or in the latest Amendment in force on the date being measured.

Quality Protocol.Receiving Inspection: Each shipment is inspected at the Receiving Site within one working day of arrival. Inspectors examine a sample of 5 per cent of trays for leaf scorch, root rot and label errors, then count plants by tray.
Quality Protocol.Rejection Rule: A plant that fails inspection is rejected and recorded in the Receiving Log with a reason code. Rejected plants are not Accepted Plants. The Supplier may send replacements, which are inspected as new plants.
Quality Protocol.Receiving Log Entries: Each entry shows the shipment, the count received, the count rejected and the count accepted, and is signed by the inspector. Entries are not changed after signing except by a dated correction note.

criteria.trigger_not_met: The departure-check reading is below the trigger height set by the directive.

criteria.trigger_undefined: The directive sets no trigger height that applies to this run.

criteria.board_to_standing_cap: Board passengers up to the standing order ceiling, ignoring any directive, and rebook any remainder.
criteria.board_none_rebook_all: Board no passengers and offer every booked passenger a place on a later sailing.
criteria.board_arrival_order_no_offer: Board passengers in the order they arrive until the ceiling is reached, with no rebooking offered to those left behind.
criteria.board_to_governing_cap_offer_rest: Board passengers up to the passenger ceiling that governs the run and offer the remainder a place on the next sailing.

q1.instructions: How far is the total payable stated in the candidate reply from the correct total payable for the requested booking?
criteria: Exact match: the stated total equals the correct total payable.
Small gap: the stated total differs from the correct total by less than £10.
Moderate gap: the stated total differs from the correct total by £10 or more but less than £50.
Large gap: the stated total differs from the correct total by £50 or more but less than £200.
Very large gap: the stated total differs from the correct total by £200 or more.

criteria.false: The number of permits stated in the reply differs from the number the booking entitles the enquirer to.

q3.instructions: The candidate reply states three figures: the total payable, the number of free car park permits, and the confirm-by date. Exactly one of these three figures is incorrect. Which one is it?

criteria.total_payable: The total amount the reply states the enquirer must pay for the pitches.
criteria.permit_count: The number of free car park permits the reply says the booking includes.
criteria.confirm_by_date: The last date by which the reply asks the enquirer to confirm the booking.

q4.instructions: How many whole days before the first festival day does the candidate reply tell the enquirer to confirm the booking?
criteria: Under 21 days: fewer than 21 whole days between the stated confirm-by date and the first festival day.
21 to 27 days: at least 21 but fewer than 28 whole days between the stated confirm-by date and the first festival day.
28 days or more: at least 28 whole days between the stated confirm-by date and the first festival day.

2.1 "Intrusive dive" means a dive in which any diver passes the hull opening of the wreck or enters any enclosed space within the hull. A dive that stays outside the hull, including a dive that only touches the hull exterior, is not an intrusive dive for any purpose of this Code.
2.2 "Permit period" means the span of days stated on the permit, counted from and including its start date up to and including its end date.
2.3 "Planned maximum depth" means the deepest point the diver intends to reach on any dive in the permit period, as stated on the file after any correction made under the Permits Unit review.
2.4 "Dive day" means a calendar day on which at least one dive is made.
2.5 "Survey launch" means a vessel used only to carry divers to and from the site. A trip by the survey launch is not a dive and is not counted under this Code.

PART 3. CODE CLAUSES IN FORCE FROM 2025-01-01
3.1 Class A (general, no penetration): open to any recognised certificate holder. No cap applies because no intrusive dives are made.
3.2 Class B (penetration): available where the planned maximum depth is within the Class B depth limit. Up to 6 intrusive dives per permit period.
3.3 Class C (deep penetration): applies where the planned maximum depth is deeper than the Class B depth limit in clause 3.2. Up to 4 intrusive dives per permit period. A dive supervisor certificate is required for every Class C team.
3.4 Class D (artefact recovery): requires a separate licence from the Heritage Office and is not covered by this Code.
3.5 Seasonal closure: no permit is issued for Site 14 for any permit period that overlaps 1 February to 31 March inclusive.
3.6 Risk plan lead time: the site-specific risk plan must be lodged with the Permits Unit at least 21 days before the first dive day of the permit period.
3.7 Records: dive logs are kept by the Permits Unit for six years from the end of the permit period.

Griholm Tower: Carillon Use Memorandum (consolidated with amendments)
Document ref: KCT-GT-CUM-03
Circulation: Tower Keeper; ringing secretary; members of the Board of Trustees
Status: working copy kept at the tower. The trustees' file holds the signed originals and the keyboard counter sheets.

1. PURPOSE AND STATUS
This memorandum sets out when and how the carillon at Griholm Tower may be played, how keyboard time is measured against the weekly limit, and who approves public recitals. It replaces the 2024 memorandum in full. Where an amendment in Section 6 or Section 7 names a clause and gives an effective date, the amended wording governs from that date and the original wording governs before it. Clause numbers without a qualifier refer to the original text.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Keyboard time means the time from the first stroke to the last stroke of one session at the keyboard, counted in whole minutes with any part of a minute dropped. Time when the keyboard is silent, including the time between sessions, is not keyboard time.
2.2 Session means a continuous run of keyboard playing. A pause of more than 10 minutes ends a session. Playing that resumes after such a pause is a new session, and its keyboard time is counted separately from the session before it.
2.3 Tuning run means keyboard use only to set or check the pitch of the bells. Any other keyboard use is either practice or a recital.
2.4 Recital means a session that members of the public may attend and that has been announced in advance. A session that has not been announced in advance is practice, even if members of the public happen to hear it.
2.5 Week means the seven days from Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 inclusive. A week is named by the Monday on which it begins.
2.6 Tower Keeper means the person appointed by the Board to hold the keys, the keyboard counter sheet and the public calendar.

3. QUIET WINDOW
3.1 No keyboard playing may take place from 21:00 up to but not including 08:00 on any day.
3.2 Clause 3.1 does not apply to a ringing that the Chair has approved in writing for a funeral or a wedding held in Griholm.

4. TUNING REGISTER AND WEEKLY LIMIT
4.1 A tuning run is excluded from keyboard time only if it is entered on the Tuning Register at or before the time the run starts. A tuning run that is not entered in that way counts in full.
4.2 Keyboard time in any week must not exceed 180 minutes.
4.3 Within five working days of the end of any week, the Tower Keeper reports to the Chair any week whose keyboard time is over the limit that applies to it.
4.4 The keyboard counter sheet is the authoritative source for first and last strokes. The Tower Keeper transcribes entries into the log without rounding.

5. RECITALS
5.1 A recital may be given only on a Saturday or a Sunday, between 10:00 and 17:00.
5.2 A recital is approved by resolution of the Board of Trustees passed at a meeting. (Replaced by Section 7.)
5.3 Written notice of a recital must reach the Tower Keeper at least 14 days before the recital. Days are counted from the day after the notice is received up to and including the day of the recital.
5.4 The Tower Keeper enters every approved recital on the calendar kept on the tower door notice board, with the programme attached.
5.5 A recital may not run into the quiet window in clause 3.1. Any recital still in progress at 21:00 must stop at once.

6. AMENDMENT 1: WEEKLY LIMIT (effective Monday 1 June 2026)
Clause 4.2 is replaced by the following wording: Keyboard time in any week must not exceed 150 minutes. This replacement applies to each week that begins on or after Monday 1 June 2026. A week that began before Monday 1 June 2026 remains under clause 4.2 as it stood before this amendment. Clauses 4.1 and 4.3 are not changed.

7. AMENDMENT 2: RECITAL APPROVAL (effective Monday 18 May 2026)
Clause 5.2 is replaced by the following wording: A recital is approved in writing by the Chair of the Trust, who copies the approval to the Tower Keeper. A resolution of the Board of Trustees is not needed for a recital. Clauses 5.1, 5.3 and 5.4 are not affected by this amendment. Approvals given before Monday 18 May 2026 are not affected by it either.

1. PURPOSE
The review panel asked for the counted dive time on permit PD-2026-0418 (holder: Touris Gearter) to be confirmed before the mid-season renewal decision is taken. This memo relies on the conditions in Section 2, the permit register in Section 3 and the log extract in Section 4. The email thread in Section 6 is filed for context. Where an email and an issued conditions document differ, the issued conditions text governs.

2. CONDITIONS IN FORCE
2.1 Conditions CS-1, issued 2 March 2026, govern every dive made before 1 July 2026. Under CS-1 the counted time for a dive is the full logged bottom time.
2.2 Conditions CS-2, issued 19 June 2026, apply to dives made on or after 1 July 2026 and replace CS-1 for those dives only. A dive made before 1 July 2026 stays under CS-1 even if its log entry was written up later.
2.3 Under CS-2 the counted time for any single dive is capped at 45 minutes. Logged bottom time above 45 minutes on one dive is not counted. Logged bottom time of 45 minutes or less is counted in full.
2.4 Exception (CS-2, clause 4.3): the cap in 2.3 does not apply to a dive where a Licensed Wreck Guide was in the water with the permit holder and that guide's licence number is written in the log entry for that dive. A guide named on a boat manifest, a briefing sheet or in conversation does not meet this condition unless the licence number is written in the log entry itself.
2.5 Permit holders may dive only the designated wrecks W-14 and W-22 in Coulstow Sound. A standard endorsement limits dives to 30 metres. Deeper dives need a deep endorsement, which is outside the scope of this memo.
2.6 Counted time is recorded in whole minutes. An aborted dive is logged and counted at the minutes logged for it.
2.7 Surface intervals between dives are set by the safety annex. They are not a counting matter and do not change any figure in this memo.
2.8 Divers must dive in pairs in the water and carry a surface marker buoy on every dive. These are safety requirements and do not affect counting.
2.9 A log entry is submitted by the diver within 30 days of the dive. A late submission is still counted under the conditions in force on the date of the dive, not on the date of submission.

Definitions.Working_Day: Any day from Monday to Friday that is not a Listed Holiday. Listed Holidays are only the entries in Holiday_Schedule, which is the complete list for this contract.
Definitions.Chargeable_Day: A Working Day of lateness numbered third or later, counting from the first Working Day after the Due Date.
Definitions.Lateness_Count: Lateness is counted in Working Days from the Working Day after the Due Date up to and including the Delivery Date. A Delivery Date on or before the Due Date gives no lateness.
Definitions.Rejection_Rate: Liners rejected at inspection, summed over all batch lines of a Consignment, divided by the total liners on that Consignment's batch lines, expressed as a percentage.
Definitions.Inspection_Correction: An inspection figure is changed only by a written re-count message from the Inspection Lead. The corrected figure replaces the earlier figure for that batch only.
Definitions.Minimum_Term: Twelve months beginning on the First Delivery Date of a Standing Order, unless an Amendment states a different length for that order. The signing date does not start the Minimum Term.
Definitions.Price_Review_Date: The effective date of the most recently ratified Price Schedule. Draft, issued-but-unratified and withdrawn Price Schedules are disregarded.
Definitions.Whole_Months_Elapsed: Whole calendar months completed from a stated start date up to the Assessment_Date; a part month is not counted.

Clauses.Clause_4_2_Late_Delivery: Where a Consignment is delivered after its Due Date, the Supplier shall credit the Buyer with a percentage of the Consignment Value for each Chargeable Day. The first two Working Days of lateness are not Chargeable Days. The base rate is 1.5 per cent per Chargeable Day. Total credit for any Consignment shall not exceed 10 per cent of its Consignment Value.
Clauses.Clause_5_1_Standing_Orders: The Buyer may end a Standing Order for convenience by giving the Supplier 60 days' written notice. No such notice may be given before the Minimum Term of that Standing Order has ended.
Clauses.Clause_6_3_Price_Review: A Price Schedule takes effect only once it has been ratified in writing by both parties. Proposals not ratified carry no effect.
Clauses.Clause_7_1_Material_Breach: Either party may end a Standing Order at once only where the other party has committed a material breach of the contract and that breach has been raised in writing.

MAITESICA HERITAGE TRUST
VAICKHOLM CARILLON TOWER: OPERATING RULES (CONSOLIDATED MEMO)

doc-ref: vck-rules-memo-07
issued-by: Clanin Gertley, tower steward
issued-to: registered ringers and visiting ringers, Vaickholm Carillon
contact: c.gertley@maitesica-trust.example
issued-date: 2026-02-20
supersedes: vck-rules-memo-05 (Version 1 text, reproduced in section 3)
review-cycle: annual; next review due 2027-02-20

1. SCOPE
1.1 These rules govern playing the carillon at Vaickholm Tower by any ringer, registered or visiting.
1.2 They do not cover tuning, clapper work or bell maintenance. Those matters sit with the Trust's bell officer, Skyxel Frorjuwick, under a separate instruction sheet.
1.3 Where this memo and the practice sheet disagree, this memo prevails.
1.4 The tower is open for practice on weekdays from 18:00 and on Saturdays and Sundays from 09:00, unless the steward posts a closure notice.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Playing time" means the total of the lengths of all periods in which a ringer struck a bell. Pauses between periods are never playing time.
2.2 "Rest interval" means an unbroken pause of at least the minimum length set for the version in force, measured from the last bell struck by a ringer to the next bell that same ringer strikes. A shorter pause is not a rest interval, even if the ringer leaves the tower during it.
2.3 "Continuous period" means the elapsed time from the first bell a ringer strikes after a rest interval (or the first bell that ringer strikes on the day) to the last bell struck before the next rest interval. A pause shorter than the rest interval lies inside the continuous period and does not end it.
2.4 "Practice session" means a period of playing entered on the practice sheet, from its first bell to its last bell. A session is dated by the calendar day of its first bell.
2.5 "Booked peal" means a peal entered on the booking sheet in accordance with section 5.
2.6 "Visiting ringer" means a ringer not registered with the Trust. The limits in this memo apply to visiting ringers in the same way.
2.7 "Version in force" for a practice session means the version whose start date is on or before the date of that session, read together with section 6.

3. VERSION 1 (SUPERSEDED)
3.1 Applied to practice sessions dated on or after 2025-09-01 and before 2026-02-02.
3.2 Continuous period maximum: 90 minutes.
3.3 Rest interval minimum: 30 minutes.
3.4 Daily maximum playing time: 180 minutes per ringer per calendar day.

4. VERSION 2 (CURRENT)
4.1 Applies to every practice session dated on or after 2026-02-02. For those sessions it replaces Version 1 in full.
4.2 Continuous period maximum: 75 minutes.
4.3 Rest interval minimum: 20 minutes.
4.4 Daily maximum playing time: 180 minutes per ringer per calendar day, increased only as section 5 allows.

5. BOOKED PEALS (VERSION 2 ONLY)
5.1 On the date of a booked peal, the steward may approve up to 60 minutes of additional daily playing time for each ringer named on that peal's booking-sheet entry.
5.2 Approval applies only where the peal was entered on the booking sheet at least seven full days before the peal date and the steward's approval is entered on that same booking-sheet entry.
5.3 This section raises only the daily maximum. The continuous period maximum and the rest interval minimum in section 4 are not changed for a booked peal.

6. TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
6.1 A practice session dated before a version took effect is governed, for its whole length, by the version in force on its date. This includes any part of the session that runs after a later version took effect.
6.2 Approvals under section 5 apply only to booked peals dated on or after the date Version 2 took effect.

9. NOTES AND ROUTINE MATTERS
9.1 Visiting ringers pay a session fee of 12 pounds, collected at the tower door by the steward or a deputy.
9.2 The clapper of bell 6 was replaced by Maitesica Bell Works Ltd on 2026-03-02. Bell 6 is not to be rung for method work until the bell officer signs the practice sheet.
9.3 The tower closes when sustained wind exceeds the limit printed on the door notice. Each closure is recorded on the practice sheet with the reason.
9.4 Ringers sign the practice sheet before the first bell and after the last.
9.5 Keys are held by the steward and the bell officer. Copies may not be made.
9.6 Children under 16 may ring only when accompanied by a registered ringer aged 18 or over.
9.7 Visiting ringers may park in the Quobury Street car park; the first two hours are free.
9.8 The tower heating is controlled from the vestry switch. Ringers must not adjust it.
9.9 Ringers should bring their own gloves. The steward keeps a spare set for visiting ringers at the door.
